messages:
jess: Hey team, requests from our web app started returning 401 invalid_api_key about ~30m ago. We didn't change the key in the backend. Can you help?

leo: Hi jess — can you paste a redacted raw request header from the browser/network tab (just the Authorization header, no full key) so we can see exact formatting?

jess: Sure, here's what the devtools shows (I replaced middle chars with ...):
Authorization: \"Bearer sk_live_abc123...xyz\"

leo: That looks like the header value is wrapped in quotes. Are you doing any JSON encoding when you set headers in your client?

jess: We did a refactor yesterday to ensure headers survive middleware and I think I wrapped values with JSON.stringify. Example:
```js
// simplified
fetch('/api', {
  headers: {
    Authorization: JSON.stringify(`Bearer ${API_KEY}`),
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  }
})
```

leo: Yep — JSON.stringify will add literal quotes around the header value so the server receives Authorization: \"Bearer ...\". Redwood expects a bare token (no quotes) so the token is treated as malformed -> 401.

jess: Ugh. Trying to remove the stringify now and redeploy the small client change.

jess: (30s) Removing JSON.stringify fixed it, calls now return 200 and the app is back to normal. Thanks! :relieved:

leo: Great to hear. As a precaution rotate the key that was potentially logged/exposed and update the client to use the raw string. Also consider a quick grep/lint rule to prevent JSON.stringify on auth headers.

alex: Adding an SRE runbook note: when you see repeated 401 invalid_api_key, check network traces for quoted header values or JSON-encoded auth. We'll add a one-liner to KB and a diagnostic curl snippet that support can run.

leo: repro steps we used: 1) confirm browser Network header shows the quotes; 2) reproduce locally by setting header to '"Bearer ..."' and verifying 401; 3) change to unquoted 'Bearer ...' -> 200. Example curl to validate:
```bash
# bad (will 401)
curl -i -H 'Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_EXPOSED"' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

# good (200)
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_test_EXPOSED' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

support-bot: Closed - user confirmed repro and resolution :white_check_mark:
